# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

**RE: Denial of Lower Back Disc Surgery / Decompression (CPT 63030)**
**Member: Reese Carter | Member ID: W769161738**
**Reference Number: POC-9992A0803A-86478**
**Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-17**
**Plan: Molina Healthcare (Commercial/ACA), Wisconsin**

To Molina Healthcare Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for lower back disc surgery / decompression (CPT 63030). I am asking that this decision be reconsidered.

## Why I am appealing

My denial notice states that the request was denied because "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." I do not believe this reflects the complete record that was available, and I am asking Molina to review the following documented facts:

- I have had 18 months of progressive lower back pain that has not improved with rest.
- I completed 18 supervised physical therapy visits over 10 weeks (2026-04-24 to 2026-07-03), including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility work, documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- I used NSAIDs for 4 months without adequate relief.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-07, which gave only 3 weeks of partial relief.
- An MRI of my lumbar spine on 2026-06-23 showed an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root.
- I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes, and I have radicular pain radiating into my right calf.
- On examination, I had positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the level shown on imaging.
- I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I do not smoke.
- My surgeon, Dr. Reyes, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary based on this history, imaging, and exam findings.

This is a substantial clinical record covering symptom duration, conservative treatment, imaging, and functional and neurologic findings. If Molina's reviewers found the submission incomplete, I am asking that Molina identify specifically what documentation is considered missing so that my provider's office can supply it, rather than have the request denied outright.

## Request for the criteria applied to my case

I understand that Molina's utilization management review is based on MCG criteria, which are available to providers through the secure provider portal, and that members may also request in writing the specific criteria used to reach a determination. I am formally requesting that Molina provide, in writing, the MCG guideline title and the specific criteria applied to my determination, so that I and my surgeon can review exactly what standard was used and respond to it directly. Because Molina's own policy citations were not included or quoted in my denial notice, I am unable to address specific criteria language here, and I am asking Molina to supply it.

## What I am requesting

1. Reconsideration of the denial of CPT 63030 based on the clinical documentation summarized above.
2. A written statement identifying exactly what documentation, if any, is still considered incomplete or missing.
3. Written disclosure of the MCG guideline title and criteria applied to my determination.

I understand my appeal must be received by 2027-02-13. I will submit this appeal to the address printed on my denial notice, and I may also follow up through the Molina member portal at molinahealthcare.com or by calling the Member Services number on my ID card.

Please contact me if any additional information is needed.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Reese Carter
Member ID: W769161738
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
Date: [date of submission]
